population_note: 2017 Population and Housing Census, from the dzongkhag's own report, counting everyone found there 'irrespective of their nationality' as the report puts it. Bhutan's census does not ask religion, language or ethnicity, so those three are declared rather than left empty. Note that the dzongkhag reports and the national report do not agree everywhere: the twenty come to 720,837 against the 727,145 the national report analyses, itself 8,408 short of the 735,553 found in the country once non-Bhutanese in hotels are counted. The figure here is the dzongkhag's own, which its gewogs add up to exactly. Of these, 6,636 are counted in Bumthang Town, Chhumig Town, which the boundary file does not draw, so the gewogs below come to that much less than this row.
sex_ratio_note: Females per 1,000 males, derived from the Male and Female columns of the same Table 2.1 row as the population beside it. The census counts sex and nothing else about identity, so this is the whole of what it says about who these people are.

population_note: 2017 Population and Housing Census, from the dzongkhag's own report, counting everyone found there 'irrespective of their nationality' as the report puts it. Bhutan's census does not ask religion, language or ethnicity, so those three are declared rather than left empty. Note that the dzongkhag reports and the national report do not agree everywhere: the twenty come to 720,837 against the 727,145 the national report analyses, itself 8,408 short of the 735,553 found in the country once non-Bhutanese in hotels are counted. The figure here is the dzongkhag's own, which its gewogs add up to exactly. This is the gewog's own count. Towns and thromdes are enumerated beside the gewogs rather than inside them and the boundary file draws none of them, so a dzongkhag's gewogs come to less than the dzongkhag itself by its urban population -- 37.8% of Bhutan nationally, and named on the dzongkhag's record.
sex_ratio_note: Females per 1,000 males, derived from the Male and Female columns of the same Table 2.1 row as the population beside it. The census counts sex and nothing else about identity, so this is the whole of what it says about who these people are.

population_note: 2017 Population and Housing Census, from the dzongkhag's own report, counting everyone found there 'irrespective of their nationality' as the report puts it. Bhutan's census does not ask religion, language or ethnicity, so those three are declared rather than left empty. Note that the dzongkhag reports and the national report do not agree everywhere: the twenty come to 720,837 against the 727,145 the national report analyses, itself 8,408 short of the 735,553 found in the country once non-Bhutanese in hotels are counted. The figure here is the dzongkhag's own, which its gewogs add up to exactly. This is the gewog's own count. Towns and thromdes are enumerated beside the gewogs rather than inside them and the boundary file draws none of them, so a dzongkhag's gewogs come to less than the dzongkhag itself by its urban population -- 37.8% of Bhutan nationally, and named on the dzongkhag's record.
sex_ratio_note: Females per 1,000 males, derived from the Male and Female columns of the same Table 2.1 row as the population beside it. The census counts sex and nothing else about identity, so this is the whole of what it says about who these people are.

population_note: 2017 Population and Housing Census, from the dzongkhag's own report, counting everyone found there 'irrespective of their nationality' as the report puts it. Bhutan's census does not ask religion, language or ethnicity, so those three are declared rather than left empty. Note that the dzongkhag reports and the national report do not agree everywhere: the twenty come to 720,837 against the 727,145 the national report analyses, itself 8,408 short of the 735,553 found in the country once non-Bhutanese in hotels are counted. The figure here is the dzongkhag's own, which its gewogs add up to exactly. This is the gewog's own count. Towns and thromdes are enumerated beside the gewogs rather than inside them and the boundary file draws none of them, so a dzongkhag's gewogs come to less than the dzongkhag itself by its urban population -- 37.8% of Bhutan nationally, and named on the dzongkhag's record. The boundary file draws this gewog as Dagala. This gewog has no reference point to place it with, so the polygon was identified by elimination: every other gewog of Thimphu is matched, and this is the one polygon and the one gewog left.
sex_ratio_note: Females per 1,000 males, derived from the Male and Female columns of the same Table 2.1 row as the population beside it. The census counts sex and nothing else about identity, so this is the whole of what it says about who these people are.
